issues.description: The problem statement and UML expect Stock to provide an addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) method, and the solution implements addToStockIngredients, but the template Stock class instead defines addItem(StockIngredient). This name/signature mismatch can confuse students when they implement SealSaloon (which will call addToStockIngredients as described) because the template does not provide the expected method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution by renaming the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or alternatively update the problem statement/UML to refer to addItem). Ensure the method signature and visibility match the UML and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution use the Stock method name addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), while the template implementation declares this operation as addItem(StockIngredient). This mismatch means students reading the task (which names addToStockIngredients) may not find the expected method in the starter code, creating unnecessary mapping confusion between the required API and the provided template.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template's Stock.addItem(StockIngredient) method to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) to match the problem statement and the solution. Alternatively, update the problem statement to accept addItem if that name is intentional, but aligning the template to the documented API will reduce student confusion.
